passages.text: “Do not judge, or you will be judged.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
He teaches about judgment.
He says, "Do not judge."
If you judge others, you will be judged.
passages.original: Μὴ κρίνετε ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε

passages.text: For with the same judgment you pronounce, you will be judged; and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about judging others.
He said, “God will judge you by the same standard you use to judge others.”
If you judge someone, God will judge you in the same way.
If you measure others, God will measure you with the same measure.
Your actions toward others will return to you in the same way.
passages.original: ἐν ᾧ γὰρ κρίματι κρίνετε κριθήσεσθε καὶ ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν

passages.text: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
He teaches about judging others.
You see a small speck in your brother’s eye.
You do not notice the large beam in your own eye.
You focus on your brother’s small fault.
You ignore your own greater fault.
passages.original: Τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου τὴν δὲ ἐν τῷ σῷ ὀφθαλμῷ δοκὸν οὐ κατανοεῖς

passages.text: How can you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while there is still a beam in your own eye?
passages.sermon:
Jesus teaches about judging others.
He speaks to people who notice faults in others.
He says, “How can you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye’?”
You still have a beam in your own eye.
You should not try to correct your brother while you have a greater fault yourself.
passages.original: ἢ πῶς ἐρεῖς τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου Ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σου καὶ ἰδοὺ ἡ δοκὸς ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ

passages.text: You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to people who judged others but ignored their own faults.
He called such people hypocrites.
He said, “You must first remove the beam from your own eye.”
After you remove the beam from your own eye, you will see clearly.
Then you can remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
passages.original: ὑποκριτά ἔκβαλε πρῶτον ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ τὴν δοκόν καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις ἐκβαλεῖν τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου

passages.text: Do not give dogs what is holy; do not throw your pearls before swine. If you do, they may trample them under their feet, and then turn and tear you to pieces.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He warned them about sharing holy things.
Do not give what is holy to dogs.
Do not throw your pearls in front of pigs.
If you do, the pigs may trample the pearls under their feet.
Then the pigs may turn and attack you.
passages.original: Μὴ δῶτε τὸ ἅγιον τοῖς κυσίν μηδὲ βάλητε τοὺς μαργαρίτας ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων μή‿ ποτε καταπατήσουσιν αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτῶν καὶ στραφέντες ῥήξωσιν ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
He teaches them about prayer.
He says, “Ask, and God will give to you.”
He says, “Seek, and you will find.”
He says, “Knock, and God will open the door for you.”
passages.original: Αἰτεῖτε καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν ζητεῖτε καὶ εὑρήσετε κρούετε καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν

passages.text: For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.
passages.sermon:
God listens to people who ask Him.
Everyone who asks receives from God.
Everyone who seeks finds what they are looking for.
Everyone who knocks will have the door opened to them by God.
passages.original: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται

passages.text: Which of you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He taught them about God the Father.
He said, “Suppose you are a father.
Your son comes to you.
He asks you for bread.
You will not give him a stone.
No father would do that.”
passages.original: Ἢ τίς ἐστιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος ὃν αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἄρτον μὴ λίθον ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ

passages.text: Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?
passages.sermon:
A father cares for his child.
A son may ask his father for a fish.
The father will not give his son a snake instead.
A good father gives what is good to his child.
passages.original: ἢ καὶ ἰχθὺν αἰτήσει μὴ ὄφιν ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ

passages.text: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him!
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said that people are sinful.
Even sinful people know how to give good gifts to their children.
God is your Father in heaven.
God is not sinful.
God is perfectly good.
God gives good things to those who ask Him.
God gives even better gifts than people do.
God gives good things to His children who pray to Him.
passages.original: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὄντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς δώσει ἀγαθὰ τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν

passages.text: In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you. For this is the essence of the Law and the Prophets.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
He teaches them how to live.
He says, “Do to other people what you want them to do to you.”
He tells them to act kindly and fairly to everyone.
He explains, “This command sums up the Law and the Prophets.”
He means that this rule is the heart of God’s commands in Scripture.
passages.original: Πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν θέλητε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται

passages.text: Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to the people.
He tells them to enter through the narrow gate.
The narrow gate is hard to find.
The wide gate is easy to find.
The broad road leads to destruction.
Many people go through the wide gate.
Few people find the narrow gate.
passages.original: Εἰσέλθατε διὰ τῆς στενῆς πύλης ὅτι πλατεῖα ἡ πύλη καὶ εὐρύχωρος ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ἀπώλειαν καὶ πολλοί εἰσιν οἱ εἰσερχόμενοι δι’ αὐτῆς

passages.text: But small is the gate and narrow the way that leads to life, and only a few find it.
passages.sermon:
The gate to life is small.
The way to life is narrow.
This way leads to true life.
Only a few people find this way.
passages.original: ὅτι στενὴ ἡ πύλη καὶ τεθλιμμένη ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ζωήν καὶ ὀλίγοι εἰσὶν οἱ εὑρίσκοντες αὐτήν

passages.text: Beware of false prophets. They come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.
passages.sermon:
False prophets exist.
False prophets come to you.
They wear sheep’s clothing.
They look harmless on the outside.
Inside, they are ravenous wolves.
They intend to harm you.
Beware of them.
passages.original: Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν ψευδοπροφητῶν οἵτινες ἔρχονται πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν ἐνδύμασιν προβάτων ἔσωθεν δέ εἰσιν λύκοι ἅρπαγες

passages.text: By their fruit you will recognize them. Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
passages.sermon:
You will recognize people by their fruit.
Fruit means the results of their actions.
You do not gather grapes from thornbushes.
You do not pick figs from thistles.
passages.original: ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς μήτι συλλέγουσιν ἀπὸ ἀκανθῶν σταφυλὰς ἢ ἀπὸ τριβόλων σῦκα

passages.text: Likewise, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.
passages.sermon: A good tree always produces good fruit.\r\nA bad tree always produces bad fruit.
passages.original: οὕτως πᾶν δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖ τὸ δὲ σαπρὸν δένδρον καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖ

passages.text: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit.
passages.sermon: A good tree cannot produce bad fruit.\r\nA bad tree cannot produce good fruit.
passages.original: οὐ δύναται δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖν οὐδὲ δένδρον σαπρὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖν

passages.text: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
passages.sermon:
A tree stands in a field.
This tree does not bear good fruit.
People cut down this tree.
They throw the tree into the fire.
passages.original: πᾶν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται

passages.text: So then, by their fruit you will recognize them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
He teaches about people and their actions.
You can recognize people by their actions.
Their actions are like fruit from a tree.
Good people produce good actions.
Bad people produce bad actions.
You will know who they are by what they do.
passages.original: ἄρα¦γε ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς

passages.text: Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only he who does the will of My Father in heaven.
passages.sermon: Jesus speaks to His followers.\r\nJesus says, “Not everyone who calls Me ‘Lord, Lord’ will enter the kingdom of heaven.\r\nOnly the person who does the will of My Father in heaven will enter the kingdom of heaven.”
passages.original: Οὐ πᾶς ὁ λέγων μοι Κύριε Κύριε εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀλλ’ ὁ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς

passages.text: Many will say to Me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, and in Your name drive out demons and perform many miracles?’
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking about the final day of judgment.
Many people will speak to Jesus on that day.
They will say, “Lord, Lord.”
They will say, “Did we not prophesy in Your name?”
They will say, “Did we not drive out demons in Your name?”
They will say, “Did we not do many miracles in Your name?”
passages.original: πολλοὶ ἐροῦσίν μοι ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ Κύριε Κύριε οὐ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι ἐπροφητεύσαμεν καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δαιμόνια ἐξεβάλομεν καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δυνάμεις πολλὰς ἐποιήσαμεν

passages.text: Then I will tell them plainly, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you workers of lawlessness!’
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to people who claim to follow Him.
He says to them directly, "I never knew you."
He commands them, "Depart from Me."
He calls them workers of lawlessness.
passages.original: καὶ τότε ὁμολογήσω αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὐδέποτε ἔγνων ὑμᾶς ἀποχωρεῖτε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν ἀνομίαν

passages.text: Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to the people.
Jesus gives a teaching.
Anyone can hear the words of Jesus.
Some people hear the words of Jesus.
Some people do what Jesus says.
A person who hears and obeys Jesus is like a wise man.
A wise man builds his house on a rock.
The wise man chooses a strong foundation.
The house stands firm because it is on the rock.
passages.original: Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ἀκούει μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ ποιεῖ αὐτούς ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ φρονίμῳ ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν

passages.text: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock.
passages.sermon:
Rain fell.
Floods came.
Winds blew.
The winds struck that house.
The house did not fall.
The house stood firm.
Its foundation was on the rock.
passages.original: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέπεσαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ καὶ οὐκ ἔπεσεν τεθεμελίωτο γὰρ ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν

passages.text: But everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus gave them important teachings.
Some people hear the words of Jesus.
These people do not do what Jesus says.
A person who hears but does not obey is like a foolish man.
This foolish man built his house on sand.
passages.original: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἀκούων μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ μὴ ποιῶν αὐτοὺς ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ μωρῷ ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον

passages.text: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell—and great was its collapse!”
passages.sermon:
The rain fell.
The torrents raged.
The winds blew.
The winds beat against that house.
The house fell.
Its collapse was great.
passages.original: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέκοψαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ καὶ ἔπεσεν καὶ ἦν ἡ πτῶσις αὐτῆς μεγάλη

passages.text: When Jesus had finished saying these things, the crowds were astonished at His teaching, because He taught as one who had authority, and not as their scribes.
passages.sermon:
Jesus finished saying these things.
The crowds listened to Jesus.
The crowds were astonished at His teaching.
Jesus taught with authority.
The scribes did not teach with authority.
Jesus was different from their scribes.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς λόγους τούτους ἐξεπλήσσοντο οἱ ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ ἦν γὰρ διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν
